statement: You are given a grid of rows × cols cells that starts as all water, and a list operations of [row, col] positions. Each operation turns that cell into land.
An island is a group of land cells joined horizontally or vertically. After each operation, count the islands.
Return the list of island counts, one per operation, in order.

examples.explanation: (0, 1) joins the island at (0, 0). (1, 2) and (2, 1) touch no land on any side, so each starts a new island.
(0, 0) and (1, 1) touch only at a corner, so there are 2 islands. (0, 1) is next to both and merges them into 1, and (1, 0) just joins that island.
The two land cells are diagonal neighbours, which do not connect, so the count rises to 2.
